source.citation: Prete et al., ACS Applied Energy Materials 4(7), 6562-6573 (2021)
source.source_type: peer-reviewed article; accepted manuscript used for source checking; PDF is linked but not redistributed in this package

reported_observations.recovery_after_OC_aging: At T60, OC-aged devices show no recovery within 22 h and instead exhibit a drop-in-dark decrease, mainly in FF, with an S-shaped J-V curve appearing at 1.5 h.
reported_observations.recovery_after_SC_aging: At T60, SC-aged devices recover fully during dark storage.
reported_observations.transient_photoluminescence: The weighted-average trPL lifetime recovers during dark storage for both OC- and SC-aged devices, while OC-aged device PCE continues to decrease.
reported_observations.trpl_caveat: The paper measures trPL on the full device stack and explicitly notes that charge extraction and other processes complicate interpretation; full-stack trPL alone is not a clean measure of intrinsic bulk recombination.
reported_observations.tof_sims: Li is detected throughout even fresh devices; degradation causes further redistribution under both OC and SC. Relative Li concentration near the electron-transport interface is largest after OC degradation. Au migrates through Spiro-OMeTAD into the perovskite under both conditions, more severely under SC.
reported_observations.tof_sims_sample_caveat: The ToF-SIMS samples were separately prepared, non-encapsulated devices. The paper's SIMS profiles compare approximately OC-to-T50 and SC-to-T30 samples, not the encapsulated T60 devices used for the main J-V recovery experiment.
reported_observations.tof_sims_timing_caveat: SIMS was performed many hours after light degradation; the authors note that the observed Li distribution may reflect little or no back-migration and cannot resolve the full transient trajectory.
reported_observations.recovery_bias: A -0.5 V bias applied for the first 30 min of dark recovery accelerates recovery of OC-aged devices; the same treatment on a fresh device causes pronounced FF degradation. The effect depends on the degradation state and sample/batch variation.
reported_observations.model_interpretation: Drift-diffusion fits show a persistent elevated SnO2-interface defect density after OC aging, while the fitted value returns to the fresh-state value after SC recovery. These are fitted model parameters, not direct defect-density measurements.
reported_observations.oxygen_alternative: The authors discuss oxygen adsorption/desorption at the metal-oxide surface as an alternative explanation for the extraction barrier, and also discuss possible oxygen release/superoxide-related degradation. These oxygen-related pathways are proposed alternatives or additional effects, not uniquely established by the study.

measurement_caveats.model_fit_parameters: The CSV transcribes selected drift-diffusion fitted quantities from Table 1. They must not be presented as direct measurements of absolute defect concentrations.
measurement_caveats.tof_sims: Use matched sacrificial devices; do not claim repeated ToF-SIMS on the same photovoltaic device. Because the original SIMS cohort was non-encapsulated and had different T50/T30 endpoints, a new T60 SIMS cohort must independently demonstrate comparable qualitative degradation/recovery behavior.
measurement_caveats.mechanistic_status: The paper proposes a coupled SnO2 surface-defect / extrinsic Li-ion trapping explanation. It does not prove a unique causal mechanism; oxygen adsorption/desorption is explicitly discussed as an alternative or additional explanation.
